reasons: The code measures the elapsed time since the end of the youngest Chalk by taking the ICS top age (t_age) of the Maastrichtian, which directly corresponds to “time since the latter part of the Secondary period” as operationalized here, and also reports the base Campanian (b_age) for context. The ICS/Macrostrat boundary ages are the appropriate data modality for absolute geologic time to a boundary, and the analysis makes no modeling assumptions beyond reading those values. The pre-registered decision rule (supports if top Maastrichtian ≥ 225 Ma, else refutes) would clearly separate a world where the K–Pg boundary is near 300 Ma from one where it is much younger. The main caveats are the interpretive choice to anchor “latter part of the Secondary” at the end of the Maastrichtian (using only that boundary for the verdict) and the arbitrary but stated ±25% tolerance used to operationalize “roughly 300 million years or more.”
what_would_change_it: Make the anchoring explicit by deciding based on a range covering the youngest Chalk (e.g., require both base Campanian and top Maastrichtian to be within a stated band around 300 Ma), or justify and/or test sensitivity to the 25% tolerance (e.g., also report outcomes for >300 Ma only). Either change would remove the main interpretive/tolerance caveats.
